The EBV tegument is composed of the 350 kD large tegument protein BPLF1, 140 kD large tegument protein binding protein BOLF1, 15 kD myristylated protein BBLF1, 32 kD myristylated protein binding protein BGLF2, 58 kD capsid associated protein BVRF1, 58 kD packaging protein BGLF1, 27 kD palmitylated protein BSRF1, and 47 kD serine-threonine protein kinase BGLF4, which are common components of herpesvirus teguments.313 In addition, EBV has a 140 kD major tegument protein BNRF1, 19 kD BLRF2, 72 kD BRRF2, 54 kD BDLF2, and 42kD BKRF4 which are gamma herpesvirus specific.313 Cellular proteins including actin, HSP70, cofilin, β-tubulin, enolase, and Hsp90 are also significant components of the EBV tegument, potentially related to cytoplasmic re-envelopment. The major glycoprotein components of the envelope are gp350 (BLLF1), gH (BXLF2), and gB (BALF4), gp42 (BZLF2), gM (BBRF3), gp78 (BILF2), gN (BLRF1), gp150 (BDLF3), and gL (BKRF2) and were also observed in virions.313 Some EBV-encoded proteins, notably the EBNAs, LMP1, LMP2, gp64 (BILF1), BMRF2, and the homologs of HSV UL7 (BBRF2), UL14 (BGLF3), UL31, (BFLF2), and UL34 (BFRF1) were not detected in EBV virions.313
<H1>Genome structure

The EBV genome is a linear, double-stranded DNA composed of 60 mole percent guanine and cytosine.27,344 The EBV genome was the first genome fully sequenced by a conventional subcloning and Sanger sequencing strategy.27 The prototypic EBV type 1 genome DNA sequence (171,823 bp) found in NCBI (GI:82503188) is actually a composite of two viral genomes B95-8 and Raji, both of which carry deletions within the viral genome that may have occurred during passage in tissue culture (see Fig. 71.1).27,542,555 B95-8 was selected for virus production in culture and was found to be deleted for the BARTs which is discussed in the EBV miRNAs section of this chapter.594,676 B95-8 remains the most extensively studied EBV strain. P3HR1, another deletion virus, was important for the discovery of the essential role of EBNA2 before genetic manipulation with the EBV genome was possible (See EBNA2 section in this chapter) and the role of the Z protein in initiation of lytic replication (See Lytic replication in this chaper). Type 2 strains have been sequenced and the prototypic type 2 strain deposited in NCBI (AG876) is 172,760 bp and as described above is highly homologous to type 1 EBV.176 An isolate of an EBV type 1 strain (M81) has an increased ability to infect epithelial cells, reduced ability to infect B cells, and increased lytic replicaton, and has been proposed as a new EBV subtype.735 The characteristic features of EBV and most other lymphocryptovirus genomes include: (a) a single overall format and gene arrangement, (b) 2 to 5 tandem, 0.5 kbp, direct repeats of the same sequence at both termini (TR), (c) 6 to 12 tandem reiterations of a 3 kbp, internal direct repeat (IR1), (d) short and long largely unique sequence domains (US and UL) that have almost all of the genome coding capacity, (e) perfect and imperfect tandem DNA repeats, most of which are within ORFs, and (f) a duplicated region, IR2, near the left end of UL, which consists of multiple, highly conserved, G-C rich, tandem 125 bp repeats and 2 kbp of adjacent unique DNA, all of which have extensive homology to a region, IR4, near the right end of UL. IR4 is comprised of G-C rich, tandem 102 bp repeats and 1 kbp of nearby unique DNA. The IR3 and IR4 repeats are within ORFs. Because the IR3 repeat is 125 kbp and not divisible by three, sequential iterations are translated in different reading frames, resulting in an unusual protein. IR3 and IR4 also include the origins for initiation of viral DNA replication.246The reiteration frequency of the EBV tandem perfect repeats becomes variable during viral DNA replication, with the average number of repeats being identical to the parent genome and most of the progeny having similar numbers of repeats as the parental genome. When EBV infects a cell, the genome becomes an episome with a characteristic number of TRs, dependent on the number of TRs in the parental genome, and the unique cleavage and joining events of the single infecting viral genome. If infection is non-permissive for viral replication and permissive for latent infection and continued cell growth, each EBV episome in progeny infected cells will usually have the same number of TRs as the parent cell. Homogeneity or heterogeneity in the number of TRs is therefore useful in determining whether a group of latently infected cells arose from a single common progenitor infected cell or from multiple progenitors.595 The number of 3 kbp IR1 repeats also varies among EBVs and among progeny of EBV replication, but is more difficult to assess as a marker of heterogeneity because of the 18-30 kbp total size. Other, smaller, imperfect, or less highly reiterated repeats within ORFs are more stable during replication, but differ sufficiently among different virus isolates so that the size of the encoded proteins can be used to uniquely identify each isolate.
<H1>Steps in Replication
<H2>Attachment and Entry

EBV uses different glycoprotein combinations to infect B cells and epithelial cells (Fig. 71.4), but similar to other human herpesviruses, the core fusion complex consists of gB (orignally designated gp110) and gH/gL (originally designated gp85/gp25). Antibodies directed against the core EBV fusion complex can potently neutralize fusion and infection.640,680 EBV gB is the fusogen for viral entry and the gB structure is composed of trimers and is similar to the structure of HSV gB. The solved gB structure likely represents a post fusion conformation since the structure is very similar to the low-pH or post fusion form of G protein of vesicular stomatitis virus.26
<H2>B Lymphocytes

B lymphocytes and epithelial cells are the major sites for EBV infection in the human host. CD21, also known as complement receptor 2 (CR2), is critical for EBV B-cell entry. Reflecting the importance of CD21 for B cell infection, CD21 is abundantly expressed on B cells and binds the virus encoded gp350/220.201 gp350/220 has homologs in primate gamma herpesviruses, but there are no sequence related proteins in the other human herpesviruses. CD21 is expressed on a subset of mature peripheral CD3+ T cells, with a higher level of expression on the naive CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell subsets and has been shown to be an entry receptor for the virus into T-cells.678 gp350 and gp220 are encoded by the same mRNA, but a single splice generates the gp220 reading frame.287 No known distinct function of either gp350 or gp220 has been determined since they both contain the domain that binds CD21.714 CD35 also binds gp350/220 and functions to allow EBV attachment to B cells.543

CD21 is the receptor for the C3d component of complement and is part of a large family of complement regulatory proteins. Family members have one or more extracellular structural motifs known as short consensus repeats (SCR). As well as being expressed on B cells, CD21 is expressed on other cell types including tonsillar epithelial cells307 and T cells, particularly naïve cells.678 The extracellular domain of CD21 contains multiple SCRs, but only SCR-1 and SCR-2 are required for EBV and C3d binding.94,317,425 Soluble CD21 binds to the EBV virion and can block B cell infection. The structure of the key gp350 binding domain on CD21 was solved590 and the region of gp350 required for binding to CD21 is contained within a portion of gp350 that is not glycosylated.708 Compatible with this finding, deglycosylated gp350 binds to CD21 as does the fully glycosylated gp350.708

Binding of EBV virions or a soluble form of gp350 to CD21 results in capping of CD21 followed by endocytosis, indicating a putative role of signal transduction in EBV B lymphocyte entry. The binding of gp350/220 to CD21 parallels the interaction of HSV gC with cell surface proteoglycans in tethering virions to target cells. This initial step is not absolutely required for infection since EBV deleted for gp350/220 or HSV-1 deleted for gC have only modest defects in virus entry in vitro when infections are performed with high virus titers. After binding to B cells, EBV virions are endocytosed492 and fusion of the viral membrane is thought to occur via the interaction of gp42 with HLA class II followed by fusion mediated by gH/gL and gB.

HLA-DR was found to bind gp42 in an expression library screen for proteins that bound a soluble form of gp42695. Both structural and functional studies have shown that gp42 exhibits features of the C-type lectin family510,695 and has no known sequence homologs in other human herpesviruses but is found in the EBV-related primate viruses. The gp42/HLA-DR interaction is essential for EBV infection of B cells since antibodies to gp42 and HLA-DR block infection397,491. In addition, virus deleted for gp42 does not infect B cells unless soluble gp42 is provided in trans or polyethylene glycol is added to promote fusion.770 Also indicative of the important role of gp42 in B cell infection, virosomes lacking gp42 bind B cells but are unable to fuse.245 The binding site of gp42 on HLA class II has been extensively studied by mutagenesis244 and by protein crystallography.510 Specific HLA-DR alleles correlate with EBV infection and binding to gp42.396, 117 Because of the key role of in antigen presentation, studies have suggested gp42 may block HLA class II antigen presentation preventing CD4 T cell activation.604,695

gp42 stably interacts with gH/gL and links receptor binding with fusion mediated by gH/gL and gB. The structure of gp42 not bound to receptor indicates that a conformational change occurs upon binding of gp42 to HLA class II, widening a hydrophobic pocket on the surface of gp42, which suggests a conformational change is important in triggering fusion by engaging other components of the EBV fusion complex.352 The EBV gH/gL structure has also been solved467, revealing an elongated rod-like shape, with the middle being the widest and gL forming intimate contacts with the N-terminal residues of gH. These features are compatible with the known chaperone function of gL for gH expression, processing, and transport.803 Of particular interest, a KGD sequence found on the gH/gL surface is implicated in integrin binding and epithelial cell entry.467 Validating the central role of gH/gL in EBV entry, gH mutants within a gH glycosylation site, the cytoplasmic tail, or a large groove that separates domain 1 and domain 2 of gH/gL all have defects in fusion.109,110,499

The structure of gH/gL/gp42 complex bound to an anti-gH/gL antibody (E1D1) has been solved.638 In these studies, it was shown that gp42 interacts with gH/gL via two domains in the gp42 amino terminus located outside the gp42 C-type lectin domain. p42 domains cross three domains on the gH surface. Both the binding of the gp42 N-terminal domain and E1D1 to gH/gL selectively inhibit epithelial-cell fusion; however, they engage distinct surfaces of gH/gL. The extensive structural and mutational studies of EBV entry proteins has led to a model for the assembly of the putative B cell entry complex comprised of gH/gL, gp42, and HLA class II (Fig. 71.5).639 These studies provide a snapshot of an intermediate state in EBV entry and highlight the potential for the triggering complex to bring the two membrane bilayers into proximity by interactions of the constituents of the complex based on an “open” and “closed” form of the complex observed in CryoEM. These open and closed forms of resemble those previous seen in Cryo-ET studies done with HSV-1. Interestingly, in this assembled complex, gH/gL interacts with the gp42 hydrophobic pocket. This result suggests that following receptor engagement, binding of gp42 may drive fusion mediated by gH/gL and gB by bringing the viral and cellular membranes together. Previous studies indicated that a domain containing gL amino acids Q54 and K94576 is important for triggering gB and may specifically interact with EBV gB to trigger fusion (Fig. 71.5).

EBV virions produced by B cells have reduced gp42 as a consequence of gp42 binding to HLA class II, which is present in infected B cells, during lytic replication.56 EBV deficient in gp42 is defective in B cell infectivity, but is enhanced in epithelial cell infectivity.56 The absence of gp42 enables the gH/gL complex to engage an epithelial cell receptor, which is otherwise occluded by gp42. During virus egress from epithelial cells, the absence of HLA class II results in virions containing gp42 bound to gH/gL that efficiently infect B lymphocytes.
<H2>Epithelial Cells

In contrast to B cell entry, EBV entry into epithelial cells occurs at the cell surface in the absence of endocytosis.492 CD21 is expressed in tonsil epithelium, but not in epithelium from buccal mucosa, uvula, soft palate or tongue by RT-PCR suggesting that the gp350/222 interaction with CD21 may be important for epithelial cell infection.307 BMRF2 may also have a role in epithelial cell entry. BMRF2 is a multispan membrane protein that contains an extracellular RGD motif that is a ligand for 1, 5, 3 and v integrins.792 This interaction is important for infection of polarized epithelial cells737, and antibodies to BMRF2 or to 51 integrin block EBV infection of polarized epithelial cells through the basolateral cell surface. Interestingly, BMRF2 is not abundant in the EBV virion313 and appears not to have a role in fusion, so BMRF2 may function similar to gp350/220 to tether virions to target cells and to induce signal transduction pathways. Integrin signaling has been shown to be important in Kaposi sarcoma herpesvirus (KSHV) infection. Integrins V5, V6, and V8 bind to gH117, but this interaction is not required for the triggering of fusion. Earlier studies had shown that a soluble form of gH/gL bound specifically to epithelial cells, but not B cells.57 In addition, gH-null virus does not bind to epithelial cells and a monoclonal antibody to gH/gL can reduce both gH/gL and virus binding.57,500 In more recent studies, integrin V knock-out HEK293 cells were generated using the CRISPR-Cas9 system. No difference between WT HEK293 and integrin V knock-out HEK293 cells were found for viral infection or fusion activity, indicating that integrins are not essential for entry in HEK293 cells and may function as entry mediators.111 In these same studies, Ephrin A2 (EphA2) was identified as an EBV receptor for epithelial cells111, which was independently identified as an EBV receptor in a second study.812 EphA2 belongs to the largest receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) family, with 14 known human members that play roles in boundary formation, cell migration, axon guidance, synapse formation, angiogenesis, proliferation, and cell differentiation. EphA2 is also a receptor for KSHV, another human gammaherpesvirus. IFITM1 blocks EphA2-mediated entry of EBV infection into epithelial cells.802 Neuropilin 1 binds to EBV gB and serves as an entry mediator for epithelial cells via macropinocytosis and lipid raft-dependent endocytosis759, while nonmuscle myosin heavy chain IIA interacts with gH/gL and is also important for entry of the virus into epithelial cells.793 gH/gL binds to R9AP (also known as RGS9BP) which mediates fusion of the virus to both B cells and epithelial cells398.

Other modes of EBV infection may also exist for virus entry. Virus coated with IgA can bind to the polymeric IgA receptor.671 This form of infection by may be relevant in nasopharyngeal carcinoma, where high levels of EBV specific IgA antibodies are found in the blood.260 However, EBV is transcytosed in polarized epithelial cells without evidence of replication.221 Interestingly, antibodies directed against gp350/220 can enhance EBV epithelial infection independent of Fc receptor interactions, and cell contact also enhances epithelial infection.657,738 Cell-associated virus is very efficient in infecting epithelial cells or B cells. Recently, a novel mechanism for EBV infection was reported for non-susceptible epithelial cells through the formation of cell-in-cell structures.529 Epithelial CNE-2 cells that are resistant to infection were invaded by EBV-infected Akata B cells to form cell-in-cell structures in vitro. Interestingly, similar unique cellular structures were observed in biopsies of nasopharyngeal carcinoma. How these different routes of infection impact EBV infection in humans requires further investigation. Efficient spread of EBV in stratified epithelial cells is dependent on EBV BDLF2.754
<H2>EBV Latency Programs

An intriguing aspect of EBV is its ability to establish different types of latent B-cell infection. EBV switches between latency programs to navigate the B-cell compartment and to colonize memory B-cells, the reservoir for lifelong EBV infection. Up to 9 EBV proteins are expressed in EBV latency programs (see Table 71.1). These include 6 EBNAs, 2 LMPs and the viral BCL2 homologue BHRF1. Their key functions are shown in Table 71.1. EBV latency genes are conserved with closely related primate lymphocryptoviruses but not with other herpesviruses.. In addition to protein products, 2 highly abundant Epstein-Barr encoded RNAs (EBERs) and up to 44 viral miRNAs are expressed.

Following primary B cell infection, the EBV W promoter (Wp) drives transcription of a message that encodes EBNA-LP and EBNA2 (Fig. 71.6).508 While this message potentially encodes all six EBNAs, at very early time points EBNA2 and EBNA-LP are preferentially expressed. BHRF1 is also expressed at low levels, and T-cells can recognize BHRF1 epitopes in newly infected cells.64,335 A Wp upstream element recruits YY1, Pax5 and additional transcription factors that together provide B-cell tropic expression.

EBNA-LP and EBNA2 reach levels significantly higher than those observed in LCLs by 48 hours post infection508,767, contributing to major host transcriptome and proteome remodeling. At 72 hours post-infection, some infected cells rapidly proliferate.534,573,768 Together with host factors, EBNA2 activates the EBV C promoter (Cp). The Cp CBF1 region associates with RBP-J, which recruits EBNA2. The CBF2 region recruits Pax5.728 Interestingly, Cp and Wp are mutually exclusive, and post-transcriptional mechanisms represses Wp upon Cp activation.280,591

Cp and Wp regulation is complex. RBP-Jκ/CBF1 is a host sequence specific transcription factor that associates with Cp and recruits EBNA2 to this and other key DNA sites. EBNA2, EBNA-LP and EBNA1 promote Cp/Wp activity, whereas EBNA3 proteins compete with EBNA2 for binding to CBF1 to downmodulate their activity.314,458,608,609

Cp initially drives the viral latency IIb program, where an ~125 kilobase EBV transcript is alternatively spliced for expression of six EBNAs.238,250,408,567,633,694 BHRF1 is also expressed at low levels.508 EBNA3A, EBNA3B, EBNA3C and EBNA1 reach levels seen in LCLs at ~72 hours post-infection767,508. Pol II stalling at Cp promotes EBNA expression by regulating nucleosome assembly, recruiting pTEFb and maintaining Pol II C-terminal domain phosphorylation.549 EBNA1 levels increase, to assure EBV episome transmission to progeny cells and to enhance transcription from promoters around oriP (the origin for latent viral repliciation), which includes an EBNA1 dependent enhancer and an EBNA1 dependent replication origin.

Wp and Cp are each important for EBV-driven B-cell transformation in vitro. Wp is encoded within the IR-1 repeat and is therefore present in multiple copies. Deletion of a cis-regulatory element mapping to -169 to -369 base pairs upstream of the first Wp copy, which also effects Cp activity, decreases in vitro B-cell transformation efficiency. Compensatory use of downstream Wp copies allows for a reduced level of B-cell outgrowth810. Cp deletion reduces EBV B-cell transformation efficiency by >100-fold.705 LCLs derived from wild-type and Cp deletion mutant EBV have similar EBNA levels, suggesting that Wp can support EBV oncoprotein expression in the absence of Cp.728,809

Latency III, also called the EBV growth program, is defined by the viral transcripts observed in LCLs with expression of six nuclear antigens (EBNAs 1, 2, LP, 3A, 3B, 3C), three membrane antigens (LMP1, LMP2A and LMP2B), BHRF1 and non-coding RNAs.724 BNRF1 may also be expressed at low levels, as CD8+ T-cell clones against BNRF1 peptide epitopes can recognize LCLs generated from immediate early gene knockout EBV.4,6 EBNA2 activates the promoters that drive LMP1 and LMP2, whose levels increase over the first 2 weeks post-infection.508,588 NF-B, AP-2 and early B-cell factor also upregulate LMP promoters.166,520

Latency III likely serves to expand the pool of EBV-infected B-cells in vivo and drives continous LCL proliferation in tissue culture. Latency III also upregulates adhesion molecules and plasma membrane receptors that are thought to drive EBV-infected B-cells into lymph node germinal centers, possibly for memory cell differentiation. Within the germinal center, EBV-infected cells are thought to switch to the latency II program, with EBNA1, LMP1, LMP2 and non-coding RNA expression. The viral Q promoter (Qp) drives EBNA1 expression, whereas LMP promoters (LMPp) drive LMP1/2.

Latency I is expressed in memory B-cells, where EBNA1 is the only viral protein expressed (Table 71.2). Latency I is also observed in most EBV-positive Burkitt lymphomas. In latency I , EBNA1 transcription is driven by Qp, located more than 50 kb downstream from Cp.424,514,540,642,643 However, EBNA1 negatively regulates Qp, allowing low EBNA1 levels for immunoevasion.514,632 EBNA1 is not translated in resting memory cells, resulting in the latency 0 state, in which EBV evades T-cell detection in this important reservoir cell by silencing all viral encoded proteins. In up to 15% of endemic BLs, EBNA2 deleted virus is present and is associated with Wp activation, broadening the expression pattern seen in latency I.335 In addition to expressing EBNAs 1 and 3, Wp-restricted Burkitt lymphomas express BHRF1. BHRF1 interacts with pro-apoptotic BH3-only family members BIM, BID, PUMA and BAK, confers resistance to multiple apoptotic stimuli, and accelerates MYC-driven lymphomas in a mouse transgenic model.205 Elevated MYC levels repress LMP1 expression in a murine EBV-positive Burkitt lymphoma model.62

Single cell analyses highlighted that EBV drives formation of chromatin features resminiscent of dark zone, light zone and post-germinal center B-cells, even in cells in which the key germinal center master regulator BCL6 has been suppressed.152,688,689 Host transcription factors MEF2C and NRF2 (encoded by NFE2L2) are important for EBV-induced germinal center B-cell phenotypes.689 Single cell analyses also highlighted similarities between EBV-infected B-cell states and analogous secondary lymphoid tissue B-cell states, and identified a population of EBV-infected atypical memory B-cells with potential roles in immune disorders688.
<H2>Epigenetic Regulation of EBV Programs

The viral epigenetic state resets with each lytic cycle, which produces unmethylated and unchromatinized DNA.122,319 Linear EBV genomes are chromatinized and circularize early after infection.123,406,424 Multiple layers of epigenetic control enable establishment of latency, control latency program selection, and ultimately support lytic rectivation.

BZLF1 preferentially activates promoters with methylated 5′-cytosine (5mC), termed meZREs41,44,319,320, limiting leaky lytic gene expression in newly infected B-cells. DNA methylation levels progressively increase following EBV B-cell infection, with higher levels achieved over the first 50-100 cell cycles.320 The extent of methylation is limited by EBNA2, which induces the cytosine demethylase TET2. EBNA2 colocalizes with TET2, RBP-J and EBF1. TET2 depletion triggers lytic gene expression.427,783 EBV also results in hypermethylation in an oral epithelial cell infection model.48 By contrast, as detailed below, the BRLF1 immediate-early EBV transcription factor activates unmethylated sites, which facilitates induction of the lytic cycle in newly infected epithelial cells.785

Chromatinization has a key role in silencing EBV lytic genes in newly infected cells, and viral genomes are chromatinized by 48 hours post-infection.76 However, over the first days post-infection, the (virion-associated) major EBV tegument protein BNRF1 supports latency gene expression by disrupting host histone chaperone ATRX/DAXX complexes, which would otherwise deposit repressive histone 3.3 complexes onto EBV genomes.734 BNRF1 disrupts DAXX/ATRX complexes at PML bodies and is essential for EBNA2 induction.734 BNRF1 also targets SMC5/6 cohesin complexes for degradation in newly infected cells and upon lytic reactivation807. Since SMC5/6 complexes have key roles in chromosome maintenance and in DNA damage repair, this finding may likely releate to the observation that BNRF1 induces centrosome amplification, observed also at elevated levels in cells infected by wild-type but not BNRF1-deficienct EBV.660 Polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2) deposits repressive histone 3 lysine 27 trimethyl (H3K27me3) on the EBV genome, and histone 3 lysine 9 tri-methyl (H3K9me3) is also deposited.22,405,720 While BZLF1 and BRLF1 promoters are nucleosomal, open chromatin at these sites is not sufficient for lytic reactivation.149

DNA methylation exerts control over latency program selection and further suppresses lytic gene expression in B and epithelial cells.15,585,784,785,787 Lytic gene expression is further regulated by histones and histone epigenetic marks. EBV also utilizes hyper-methylation to silence host tumor suppressor genes.624 As EBV-infected B-cells enter lymphoid tissue germinal centers, Cp DNA methylation and cytokines, in particular IL-21353, may contribute to the transition from latency III to latency II (Fig. 71.7). Initiator DNA methyltransferase DNMT3B is induced in germinal center B-cells. The epigenetic enzymes UHRF1 and DNMT1, which copy methylation marks from parental to newly synthesized DNA strands, are induced in germinal center B-cells and by primary B-cell infection. It is likely that UHRF1 and DNMT1 maintain methylation marks as cells differentiate into memory B-cells with latency I expression. Latency III and lytic gene expression are de-repressed in latency I Burkitt B-cells treated with DNA hypomethylating agents or by depletion of UHRF1.243,465,610 Polycomb repressive complex I (PRC1) further controls LMP promoter activity in B-cells and may add a layer of control over latency program switching. Depletion of PRC1 subunits de-represses LMP1 and LMP2A expression in latency I Burkitt lymphoma cells, and PRC1-mediated histone 2 lysine 119 monoubiquitination (H2Ub119Ub1) repressive marks are more abundant in Burkitt cells with latency I than latency III programs243 (Fig. 71.7).

Higher order DNA structure also regulates EBV gene expression. The CCCTC-binding factor (CTCF) binds to multiple EBV genome sites to mediate long-range chromatin interactions or to insulate genome regions. CTCF binding to the EBV genome may anchor it to the nuclear matrix and direct specific chromatin architectures that can mediate alternative promoter targeting by the oriP enhancer. The oriP enhancer facultatively associates with either Cp in latency III or Qp in latency I.719 Mechanistically, CTCF participates in each of these loops, and disruption of CTCF recruitment perturbs formation of either loop, highlighting how the viral genome coopts a host three-dimensional genome organizing factor for maintenance of epigenetically stable states. Furthermore, CTCF functions as a chromatin insulator at EBV genomic sites including Qp to block epigenetic silencing and to prevent promiscuous transcription of surrounding genes. Likewise, mutagenesis studies suggest that the CTCF site upstream of Cp also has roles in B-cell latency I epigenetic reprogramming.281 CTCF activity is post-translationally regulated by the host enzyme Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP1) and by DNA methylation. CTCF and PARP1 colocalize at specific EBV genomic sites, where PARP1 stabilizes CTCF occupancy.434 PARP1 and CTCF suppress the BZLF1 promoter.

EBV-induced host transcription factor MYC occupies the EBV genome origin of lytic replication (oriLyt) sites and prevents looping of these enhancer sites to the immediate-early BZLF1 promoter.242 MYC depletion triggers EBV three-dimensional genome reorganization that juxtaposes oriLyt with the BZLF1 promoter region. Since Blimp1 suppresses MYC expression, EBV may have evolved this mechanism to sense MYC abundance and link lytic reactivation to plasma cell differentiation. Elevated MYC levels present in newly infected B-cells suppress LMP1 expression587, further highlighting the intimate relationship between MYC and EBV epigenetic regulation. Latent EBV genomes preferentially associate with human genome heterochromatin regions characterized by lower densities of coding genes and the repressive H3K9me3 mark. Upon lytic reactivation or EBNA1 depletion, EBV genomes move towards active chromatin.347,503
<H2>Latency Gene Functions
<H3>EBNA1

EBNA1 (Fig. 71.8A) is the only EBNA that directly binds DNA. To ensure replication and stable maintenance of EBV genomes, EBNA1 binds both to the viral episome and serves to tether the viral genome to host chromosomes in mitosis. EBNA1 binds to oriP, which is the viral genome origin of DNA replication in latency.602,804 Remarkably, it was subsequently discovered that oriP and EBNA1 are sufficient for partitioning of EBV genomes, or plasmids containing oriP, to progeny cells.486,527 EBNA1 and oriP maintain the EBV genome as a replicon that is copied by host machinery once per cell cycle in S-phase. Catenation of newly replicated viral genomes appears to lead to their pairing on sister chromatids, which serves to mediate equal partitioning of episomes to daughter cells.247

The oriP family of repeats (FR), dyad symmetry (DS) element, and two cis-acting elements are critical for maintanence of EBV episomes. FR serves as a ~650 bp maintenance element and an EBNA1 dependent enhancer important for Cp activity.28,220,247,339,424,570,577 FR is located ~1 kb upstream of DS and contains multiple 18 bp copies of an EBNA1 recognition sequence436,599,602 (Fig. 71.8B). The EBNA1 N-terminus binds to perichromatic regions enriched for histone methylation marks that are hallmarks of transcriptionally active regions.167 In this manner, EBNA1 tethers FR-bound episomes to condensed mitotic chromosomes. DS serves as the latency origin for episome DNA synthesis. It contains 4 EBNA1 recognition sites and a 65 bp region of dyad symmetry.760 DS is necessary for EBNA1 dependent plasmid replication.247

EBNA1 binds DNA as a homodimer (Fig. 71.8B-D). The EBNA1 dimerization domain extends from residues 504-604. Amino acids 470-503 include a helix that projects into the DNA major groove and an extended chain that moves along the minor groove and makes all the DNA sequence specific contacts. Smooth DNA bending stabilizes interactions between EBNA1 dimers.448 An extensive hydrogen bonding network connects the dimer-dimer interface, disruption of which compromises oriP-dependent plasmid replication and MCM3 complex recruitment to oriP. EBNA1 induces a strong DNA bending angle in the DS.478 The EBNA1 DNA binding domain N-terminal arm makes substantial contact with DNA as it wraps around the minor groove.478 The EBNA1 DNA-binding domain itself forms a hexameric ring, highlighting that EBNA1 dimers assemble into higher-order structures. Point mutations at the oligomeric interface destabilize higher-order complex formation, alter cooperative DNA binding, and can either positively or negatively affect EBNA1-dependent functions.164 Using a structure and fragment-based approach, small molecule inhibitors of EBNA1 DNA binding activity were identified. EBNA1 inhibitors impair LCL and EBV-infected nasopharyngeal carcinoma cell survival in vitro and xenograft models in vivo.484 EBNA1 also forms a cell cycle-dependent DNA crosslink with oriP.170 Intriguingly, the covalent attachment between EBNA1 tyrosine 518 and oriP is necessary for replication fork termination at oriP, for EBVepisome maintenance, and for establishment of LCLs.170

The repeat unit of oriP acts as an enhancer in the presence of EBNA1, which is important for latent gene transcription from Cp.215,247 Host cell factor 1 (HCF1) and octamer-binding transcription factor 2 (OCT2) cooperatively bind oriP with EBNA1 and are each important for oriP H3K4 trimethylation, Cp and Qp activity.171 HCF1 knockdown causes EBV episome loss from Burkitt lymphoma cells, suggesting a potential HCF1 episome maintenance role. EBP2 is important for interactions between EBNA1 and chromosomes in metaphase and association with metaphase chromosomes. The MCM complex associates with DS and may have roles in initiation and licensing of EBV genome replication. EBNA1 may facilitate ORC recruitment to DS by disrupting nucleosomes to provide ORC with DNA access.215 Timeless and timeless interacting proteins, which have roles in stabilizing replication forks, are also recruited to oriP.169 Timeless depletion from Burkitt cells causes loss of closed circular EBV episomes, accumulation of linear EBV DNA and double-strand breaks at oriP, suggesting an important role in replication fork stabilization in episome maintenance.169

USP7, which is a key regulator of p53 and Mdm2, stimulates EBNA1 DNA binding activity. USP7 forms ternary complex with DNA-bound EBNA1637 and is part of a histone deubiquitylating complex. USP7 depletion increases monoubiquitylated histone H2B at EBV FR and decreases its transcriptional activation activity.272 Crystallographic studies reveal that EBNA1 and p53 bind the same USP7 pocket, but that EBNA1 makes more extensive contacts with USP7. Association between EBNA1 and USP7 protects cells from apoptotic challenge by p53 depletion. EBNA1 partially protects them from p53 overexpression-driven apoptosis636. Conversely, depletion of EBNA1 in induces apoptosis in a subset of EBV-positive Burkitt cells338. USP7 and EBNA1 also have joint roles in disruption of PML nuclear bodies.215

EBNA1 deletion does not completely prevent EBV-driven B cell outgrowth or establishment of LCLs286,573, likely since at a low frequency episome integration into host chromosomes enables DNA maintenance in the absence of EBNA1. This is apparently rare, as LCLs emerge nearly 1000-fold less frequently from EBNA1 deficient virus.286 LCLs established from wild-type versus EBNA1 deletion mutant virus grow at comparable rates and each can form xenografts in SCID mice. Thus, the contribution of EBNA1 to B cell immortalization outside of activation of EBV latency genes14 and maintaining the EBV genomes in infected cells, may be limited in comparison with roles of other EBV latency oncoproteins.

A large number of putative EBNA1 host genome targets have been identified. EBNA1 ChIP-seq was used together with RNA-seq analysis following EBNA1 depletion from LCLs, Burkitt and nasopharyngeal carcinoma cells.718 Interestingly, ~1,000 host genome EBNA1 binding sites are mostly conserved across cell types, share a consensus DNA motif, and are frequently located proximal to transcription start sites, particularly at highly expressed genes.428 EBNA1 binding sites are also enriched for LINE 1 retrotransposons. The anti-apoptotic host factor survivin is upregulated by EBNA1.40 EBNA1 binds to a cluster of tandemly repeated DNA on human chromosome 11q23 with sequence reminiscent of oriP FR. Elevated levels of EBNA1 can trigger breakage at 11q23, with potential relevance to the pathogenesis of nasopharyngeal carcinoma.395 EBNA1 suppresses natural killer responses by downregulating ULBP1 and ULBP5, which are NKG2D ligands.779
<H3>EBNA2

Early studies by Elliott Kieff’s group identified a B-cell transformation incompetent, but lytic replication competent EBV strain derived from Jijoye Burkitt cells called P3HR-1.138,154-156,263,344,351,589,597 The search for the biochemical basis of the non-transforming phenotype led to the discovery and characterization of EBNA2, which is the principal ORF deleted in P3HR-1.138,154-156,263,344,351,589,597 While EBNA-LP is also truncated in P3HR-1, it was found that restoring type 1 EBV EBNA2 expression rescued P3HR-1 B-cell growth transformation.28,136,138,424 Transfection with cloned EBV DNA fragments deleted for part of the EBNA2 ORF or containing a stop codon one third of the way into the EBNA2 ORF failed to restore transforming ability. Recombinant EBVs with a nontransforming EBNA2 mutation could also be recovered by infection of EBV negative BL cells.423 EBNA2 is the only latency gene found to be essential for newly infected B-cell mitosis or outgrowth over the first 8 days of infection .573

EBNA2 typically functions as an activator of B-cell viral and host gene transcription.138,337,758 EBNA2 is the major viral transactivator of the C and LMP promoters.758 Genetic analysis identified three essential EBNA2 domains critical for LMP and C promoter upregulation (Fig. 71.9). These correspond to EBNA2 residues 1-58 or 97-210 which mediate homotypic association, amino acids 280-337 which mediate interaction with RBP-Jκ, and C-transactivation domain (TAD) residues 420-64.130,136,138,238,248,251,258,330,337,827 In B lymphocytes, the EBNA2 C-terminal transactivation domain (TAD) is nearly as strong in activation of basal reporter constructs as the core herpes simplex VP16 activation domain.136 The VP16 core 14 amino acids can substitute for the corresponding EBNA2 C-terminal transactivation domain residues in primary B lymphocyte conversion to LCLs in recombinant EBV.130 The EBNA2 C-terminal TAD recruits basal and activation associated transcription factors including TFB1/p62, TFIIB, TAF40, RPA70, TFIIH, and the histone actyltransferases CBP/P300 and PCAF337 (Fig. 71.9). An intrinsically unstructured EBNA2 region folds into a 9 amino acid alpha helix upon complex formation.101

EBNA2 is recruited to DNA through association with host transcription factors, particularly the Notch pathway sequence specific DNA binding protein RBP-Jκ/CBF1.35,238,258,312 Whereas RBP-Jκ assembles corepressor complexes in B-cells in the absence of EBNA2, EBNA2 often converts RBP-J into an activator by competing for co-repressor binding, through EBNA2 TADs, and through recruitment of co-activators, including EBNA-LP. RBP-J is critical for LCL growth and survival.443 EBNA2 is at least partially dependent on Jκ DNA sites for transactivation of Cp310, LMP1, and LMP2.225,312,382 The Cp and LMPp sites contain EBNA2 response elements that carry J DNA motifs.

EBNA2 mimics key aspects of activated Notch signalling. The EBNA2 WWP motif (Fig. 71.9) resembles a Notch intracellular domain “WFP” sequence that tightly associates with RBP-Jκ712, and EBNA2 and Notch binding to RBP-J are mutually exclusive.276 EBNA2 residues 318-327 mediate RBP-Jκ association.415 EBNA2 induces formation of new RBP-J occupied sites.426 Yet, constitutive Notch signaling cannot replace EBNA2 to maintain EBV-transformed lymphoblastoid B-cell proliferation.230,270

Microarray profiling of EBV-uninfected Burkitt cell lines with conditional EBNA2 expression identified 311 significantly EBNA2-induced genes, including CD21, CD23, CCR7, RUNX3 and CD83. Likewise, conditional EBNA2 expression identified key EBNA2 downregulated targets, including CD79B, TCL-1 and MEF2B.446,819 EBNA2 represses expression of multiple B-cell receptor pathway components, together with EBNA3, potentially to promote EBV latency.343 EBNA2 also suppresses expression of the host transcription factor CIITA to diminish HLA class II gene transcription.699 ChIP-seq identified a much larger number of host genomic sites occupied by EBNA2426,446,471,817,821, and suggested that EBNA2 subverts intrinsic B-cell transcriptional programs. Thousands of host genome sites are co-occupied by RBP-J and EBNA2 in LCLs. EBNA2 and RBP-J predominantly co-occupy intergene and intron sites, with only a small proportion of proximal to transcription start sites.241,471,821 J DNA motifs are highly enriched at EBNA2/RBP-J co-occupied sites, whereas EBF1 DNA motifs are enriched at sites occupied by EBNA2 but not RBP-JEBNA2 reorganizes genomic binding sites of RBP-Jκ and EBF1, and EBNA2-EBF1-RBP-Jκ co-occupancy appears to transcriptionally activate target genes.228,426

EBNA2 alleles differ significantly in amino acid sequence between type 1 and 2 EBV strains.138,155,606 Reconstitution of the type 2 P3HR-1 EBV strain with a type 1, but not a type 2 EBNA2 gene, yields virus that transforms B-cells as efficiently as type 1 EBV strains.138 A single EBNA2 transactivating domain amino acid at residue 442 appears to underlie this phenotype. Subsitution of type 2 serine 442 with type 1 aspartic acid confer enhanced LMP1 upregulation and type 1 transforming activity on a type 2 EBV strain.740 In contrast, recombination of cloned type 2 EBNA2 DNA in place of the P3HR-1 deletion results in deficient transformation characteristic of type 2 EBV. Type I EBNA2 more strongly induces LMP1 and only a small number of host genes more strongly induced by type 1 than type 2 EBNA2.430

Super-enhancers (SE) are particularly strong enhancers that drive expression of genes critical for cell identity and oncogenic states. EBNA2 occupied 888 SE in in LCLs.241,309,789,826 Often located far from transcriptional start sites, these SE loop to targets, including RBPJ, EBF1, BATF and RUNX3. A subset of EBNA2 SEs, termed EBV SEs, are co-occupied by EBNAs LP, 3A, 3C and LMP1-activated NF-B transcription factors.309,826 EBV SEs often loop to more than one target gene, enabling them to target 1992 sites. EBV SE targets were enriched for host genes essential for LCL growth and survival309,443, including MYC, IRF4 and CFLAR. Two EBV SEs loop to the MYC promoter from 525 and 428 kbp upstream309,789,826, and EBNA2 is important for formation of these loops in newly infected B-cells.309 EBNA2 recruits the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeler complex to MYC enhancers to promote interactions with the MYC promoter.789 Deletion of either MYC-targeting EBV SE by CRISPR genome editing diminished MYC expression and LCL proliferation.309

EBNA2 also has key roles in host metabolism pathway remodeling in newly infected B-cells, both by strongly inducing MYC and also by EBNA2 target gene regulation.767 The EBNA2 N-terminal dimerization domain associates with EBF1, which is critical for EBNA2 driven MYC upregulation.36 EBNA2 has important roles in upregulation of aerobic glycolysis (the Warburg effect) within the first days of infection.472,508,767 EBV infection also markedly remodels mitochondria, most of whose components are encoded by nuclear genes that can be regulated by EBNA and LMP signaling. Consequently, oxidative phosphorylation is also strongly upregulated in the first week post-infection and plays similarly important roles in B-cell growth transformation.

Maximal EBNA2 RNA and protein abundance is observed by 48 hours post-infection.508,756,767 Proteomic analysis highlighted that EBV strongly induces the mitochondrial one-carbon (1C) pathway within the first days of infection, reaching maximal expression levels during the period of hyperproliferation767 to convert serine into glycine, carbon units, ATP and NAD(P)H for use in anabolic reactions. EBNA2 also initiates de novo NAD biosynthesis by inducing expression of the enzyme IDO1.511 Lipid metabolism pathways are also highly induced by EBNA2, which functions with host transcription factors such as SREBP and MYC to remodel mevalonate and fatty acid synthesis pathways. EBV-induced lipid metabolism enables cross-talk between EBNA and LMP oncoproteins.768 Relatedly, EBV dynamically sensitizes newly infected B-cells to the ferroptosis programmed cell death pathway, which is triggered by lipid free radical metabolism byproducts.75
<H3>EBNA-LP

EBNA-LP is a major co-activator of EBNA2 host and viral target genes.9,218,250,538,662 EBNA-LP targets include the C and LMP1 promoters as well as a large number of host genomic sites. EBNA-LP coactivation with EBNA2 is evident in transient expression assays with artificial LMP1 promoter constructs, and in inducing the latency III program in Burkitt cells when co-expressed by gene transfer together with EBNA2. Yet, EBNA-LP does not globally co-activate EBNA2 targets.337,424

EBNA-LP is comprised of 22 and 44 amino acid regions of variable copy number, fused to 11 and 34 residue carboxy-terminal regions. These are encoded by the W1, W2, Y1 and Y2 exons, respectively (Fig. 71.10A-B). The W1 and W2 encoded regions enable homodimerization and association with the EBNA2 acidic activating domain.250,567 In newly infected B-cells, Wp drives expression of a 5′ W0 exon, which is alternatively spliced either to the W1 or to a W1′ exon and then to W2. Since W0, W1 and W2 reside within the EBV genome internal repeat 1 (IR1) region, EBNA-LP size varies between viral strains with differing IR1 copy number. Likewise, transcripts can initiate from distinct W0 exons, giving rise to EBNA-LP products of variable length early in B-cell infection. Upon the switch to Cp driven transcription, EBNA-LP mRNAs are instead comprised of 5′ C1 and C2 exons that are joined with W and Y exons.337 At least 5 W repeats are required for optimal B-cell outgrowth, at least two of which are necessary for B-cell transformation in culture.727 This requirement results from the optimization of Wp-driven transcriptional activity. Clinical EBV strains typically have at 5-8 W copies.727

EBNA2 and EBNA-LP interact in yeast two-hybrid assays86 and as recombinant proteins in vitro. However, association between wild-type EBNA-LP and EBNA2 is difficult to detect in LCL extracts. EBNA-LP can bind to and coactivate transcription through the EBNA2 acidic activating domain or through an EBNA2 N-terminal 58 amino acid domain.567 EBNA-LP potentiates EBNA2 mediated transcription from the C and LMP1 promoters in transient transfection assays with reporter constructs and also coactivates EBNA2 upregulation of LMP1 expression in type 1 EBV-infected BL cells.

EBNA-LP localizes predominantly to promyelocytic leukemia (PML) nuclear bodies and to a lesser extent in the cytosol.337 An EBNA-LP region conserved in non-human primate lymphocryptoviruses interacts with and displaces Sp100 from PML nuclear bodies.416 Sp100A mutants deleted for the PML targeting domain, which also interacts with EBNA-LP, can coactivate EBNA2 independently of EBNA-LP, suggesting that displacement of Sp100A from PML nuclear bodies is an important EBNA-LP function.416 Deletion of a Sp100A domain that interacts with the transcriptional repressor heterochromatin protein 1 (HP1) prevents Sp100A coactivation function, suggesting that EBNA-LP function may in part involve chromatin modification.416 Together with HA95, EBNA-LP also activates transcription by displacing NCoR and histone deacetylases (HDAC) from matrix associated deacetylase (MAD) bodies.580 EBNA-LP leucine rich motifs promote association with the host transcription factor YY1, which in turn supports host genomic long-range enhancer/promoter interactions and EBV driven primary B-cell transformation.78,755 ChIP-Seq identified nearly 20,000 EBNA-LP occupied host genomic regions.581 Only 29% were co-occupied by EBNA2, in large part because ~50% of EBNA-LP sites were within 2 kb of transcriptional start sites. Long-range DNA interactions may increase contact between EBNA2-bound enhancer and EBNA-LP occupied promoter sites. EBNA-LP also regulates splicing of host gene transcripts including the anti-apoptotic Bcl-xL.453

Recombinant EBV studies suggest EBNA-LP is important for B-cell transformation. Complete repair of the P3HR1-1 deletion encoding EBNA2 and the Y1/Y2 EBNA-LP exons restores B-cell immortalization, whereas repair of only EBNA2 reduces immortalization efficiency by approximately 10-fold.28,454 EBNA-LP knockout (KO) virus exhibited reduced naive B-cell transformation efficiency. Deletion of just the Y1 and Y2 exons also substantially decreased the rate of EBV-driven B-cell outgrowth.709 EBNA-LP KO EBV likewise slows outgrowth of tonsil B-cells.573 By contrast, EBNA-LP KO virus failed to establish LCLs from umbilical cord B-cells, which underwent cell death by two weeks post-infection. Absence of EBNA-LP significantly diminished recruitment of EBNA2, EBF1 and RBP-Jκ to the viral genome, but not to the EBNA2 target IL7 host target gene.709
<H3>EBNA3A, EBNA3B and EBNA3C

EBNA3 proteins have important roles in host and viral gene regulation. EBNA3s share an N-terminal homology domain, a proline rich region and repeat sequences. EBNA3C also has a putative leucine zipper that mediates association with the host transcription factor PU.1/SP1.820 EBNA3s target DNA sites through interactions with host factors, in particular RBP-J.608,609 Each EBNA3 has transcription repression activity when tethered to DNA by a heterologous GAL4 DNA binding domain.

EBNA3A, 3B and 3C genes are arranged in tandem (Fig. 71.11) and are conserved with primate lymphocryptoviruses, but do not have homology with host proteins. EBNA3 proteins are expressed from a polycistronic transcript that encodes all 6 EBNAs, that is alternatively spliced, and that is present at low abundance in LCLs.11 Wp or Cp drive expression of EBNA3 transcripts in the latency IIb and III programs, respectively. EBNA3 messages share a U exon with EBNA1 and have individual splice acceptor sites that compete with EBNA1. EBNA3 transcripts have individual downstream polyA sites. EBNA3s are expressed within 48 hours of primary B-cell infection, reaching maximal levels between 4-7 days post infection cell culture.756,767,508 EBNA3s inhibit EBNA2 activation of the Cp, which may account for the significant drop in EBNA2 expression by 96 hours post primary B-cell infection.

EBNA3s compete with EBNA2 for the same RBP-J binding surface.609,608,818 However, EBNA3s bind more tightly to RBP-Jκ725, reminiscent of the Drosophila Notch antagonist Hairless. Deletion of the EBNA3A or EBNA3C RBP-J association region abrogates their EBNA2 antagonism.461,778 Interaction between EBNA3A or 3C and RBP-J is essential for LCL growth and survival.128,388,463

EBNA3s also repress target genes through assemby of co-repressor complexes. EBNA3s associate with host co-repressors C-terminal binding protein (CtBP), Sin3A, NCoR and histone deacetylases HDAC-1 and 2.11,627 The EBNA3A and EBNA3C region that associates with CtBP1 is required for LCL growth.388,672 CtBP1 is important for LCL, but not Burkitt growth and survival.443 EBNA3A and EBNA3C recruit CtBP by mimicking “PLDLS” domains that mediate association between CtBP and transcription co-repressors. EBNA3s association with CtBP is important for the assembly of polycomb repessive complex 2 (PRC2) at target gene sites, where the histone methyl transferase subunit EZH2 deposits histone 3 lysine 27 trimethyl (H3K27me3) repressive chromatin marks.11 H3K27me3 have been identified at EBNA3A and EBNA3C occupied sites proximal to transcriptional start sites of major tumor suppressor genes, including BCL2L11.556,789 EBNA3A also associates with the histone acetylatransferase p300 and with IRF3 to limit interferon beta promoter activation and type I interferon signaling.378

ChIP-Seq has identified a wide range of EBNA3 host and viral target gene sites. >13,000 EBNA3C sites were identified in LCLs, 64% of which were at chromatin sites with activating H3K4me1 and H3K27ac enhancer marks. DNA motifs for RUNX3, BATF, IRF4, and ATF2 are enriched at these sites.308 EBNA3C ChIP-seq signals were strongest at sites with either composite BATF/IRF4 elements (also known as ATF-Interferon composite elements, or AICE) or composite SPI1/IRF4 elements (also known as ETS-Interferon composite elements, or EICE). Similarly, ChIP-seq identified 10,000 EBNA3A host genome binding sites in LCLs, 55% of which were active enhancers and 11% of which were at active or weakly active promoters.644 AICE and EICE motifs were enriched at EBNA3A occupied sites. 25% of host genomic binding sites were shared between EBNA2 and EBNA3 proteins in Burkitt lymphoma cells with latency III expression.471

EBNA3s can also serve as transcriptional activators, alone or in concert with EBNA2. EBNA3C associates with PU.1/SPI1820 and with the histone acetyltransferase p300.146 The EBNA3C leucine zipper interacts in vitro with the PU.1-Ets domain and appears to upregulate transcription through the LMP1 promoter PU.1 binding site.820 The EBNA3C effect is independent of the RBP-Jκ binding site in the LMP1 promoter and of the RBP-Jκ interaction domain in EBNA3C.820 Furthermore, EBNA3C fully coactivates with an EBNA2 mutant that does not interact with RBP-Jκ.412 Interestingly, EBNA3C associates with the host transcription repressor CtBP, which can lead either to repression or activation of host genes. In the latter case, EBNA3C is recruited to host genomic sites with pre-existing CtBP occupancy and disrupts their repression by CtBP.545 By contrast, EBNA3C promotes the ubiquitin mediated degradation of the transcription repressor BCL6 together with the host encoded E3 ligase FBXO11.703

Using EBV-negative Burkitt lymphoma cells infected by wild-type versus EBNA3 knockout EBV, microarray analysis identified >1000 host genes whose expression significantly changed with EBNA3 deficiency.780 More than one EBNA3 regulated a third of these, with EBNA3C apparently cooperating with EBNA3A, EBNA3B or both. Expression profiling identified 167 up-regulated and 129 down-regulated host genes in LCLs established from EBNA3A deficient versus wild-type virus.264 EBNA3A-regulated genes were enriched for targets previously identified as being regulated by EBNA2. Likewise, 550 host genes were at least 1.5-fold differentially regulated in LCLs with conditional EBNA3C inactivation, and these significantly overlapped with genes regulated by EBNA2 and EBNA3A.817

EBNA3A and EBNA3C, but not EBNA3B, are each important for B-cell transformation into LCLs.730,11,627 EBNA3A KO virus is attenuated for B-cell transformation and gives rise to LCLs with increased apoptosis and reduced proliferation rates.264 Conditional EBNA3C inactivation results in the accumulation of cell cycle inhibitors p16(INK4A), p14(ARF), p53 and hypophosphorylation of Rb.462,817 Similarly, EBNA3A or 3C inactivation results in active chromatin marks at the p14 and p16 encoding CDKN2A locus.308 Knockdown of p14 or p16 partially rescues LCL growth in the absence of either EBNA3A or EBNA3C.464 B-cells obtained from an individual with a homozygous CDKN2A locus deletion that causes p16 deficiency are transformed equally well by wild-type and EBNA3C deficient virus, highlighting an EBNA3C role in overcoming a p16 dependent block to B-cell proliferation 2-4 weeks post-infection.673 EBNA3C also induces transcription of the N6-methyladenosine (m6A) writer METTL14 to promote B-cell transformation.379

EBNA3A and EBNA3C have key roles in regulation of B-cell differentiation.698 B cells infected by EBNA3A and EBNA3C conditionally-inactivated virus, or virus deficient for EBNA3s altogether, initially proliferate. However, they subsequently undergo plasmablast differentiation at 20 days post-infection. This phenotype may result from EBNA3C suppression of BCL6.562 and BLIMP1. Once committed to plasmablast differentiation, re-expression of EBNA3A and EBNA3C does not rescue LCL differentiation.698 Furthermore, EBNA3A expression inhibits terminal plasma cell differentiation otherwise driven by LMP1 and supports LMP1-driven B-cell proliferation.685 EBNA3A or 3C have key roles in repressing the BCL2L11 encoded tumor suppressor BIM. EBNA3A and 3C co-occupy assemble a PRC2 repressive complex upstream of the BCL2L11 promoter.471,556,789 Inhibition of EZH2 upregulates BIM expression789, as does KO of BATF or IRF4, suggesting that they may play roles in EBNA3 recruitment to this site.443 The H3K4me3 chromatin mark, which can be found at activated promoters, does not change with H3K27me3 deposition, suggesting that bivalent chromatin is formed.673 EBNA3A also has key roles in upregulation of the anti-apoptotic MCL-1 gene to promote infected B-cell survival at early timepoints post-infection.586

The onset of EBV-induced hyperproliferation at 3 days post-infection induces DNA replication stress and the DNA damage damage response (DDR) pathway.125,534 EBNA3C suppresses the ATM/Chk2-mediated DNA damage-responsive signaling pathway in newly EBV-infected cells.125,534 The DNA damage response has an important tumor suppression role in limiting EBV-induced B-cell transformation in vitro, as inhibition of the DNA damage response pathway kinases ATM or CHK2 increased B-cell transformation efficiency.534

Functionally-important EBNA3C interactions have been defined, many of which regulate cell cycle progression, the G1/S checkpoint, and cell survival. EBNA3C binds p53 and represses its functions by interacting with the inhibitor of growth family proteins ING4 and ING5.622,626 EBNA3C recruits the ubiquitin ligase Skp1/Cul1/F-box complex resulting in ubiquitination of the cell cycle regulators Rb and p27.357,358 EBNA3C also interacts with and modulates the activity of cyclins A, D1, and E.355,356,623 EBNA3C associates with the transcription repressor E2F6 to reduce E2F1 activity.561 Furthermore, the EBNA3C N- and C-terminal domains associate with E2F1 to block its induction of apoptosis stimulated by the DNA damage response.625 EBNA3C upregulates and associates with PIM-1 kinase to down-modulate activity of the cell-cycle inhibitor p21/WAF1.32 EBNA3C also recruits Skp2 ubiquitin ligase complexes to cyclin A to target degradation of the kinase inhibitor p27 and further promote cell proliferation.358 The EBNA3C N-terminal domain associates with IRF4 and IRF8 and stabilizes IRF4. IRF4 depletion causes decreasd MYC and CDK6 expression and causes LCL death.31,443 EBNA3C induces and associates with the WTAP N6-methyladenosine transferase, which in turn regulates EBV transcript stability and promotes EBV-transformed cell growth.379

In cord blood humanized mouse models, EBNA3C deficient EBV induced lymphomas at decreased frequency and with delayed onset in comparison to wild-type virus. P16 levels were increased in tumors that arose from EBNA3C knockout virus in comparison to wild-type virus-infected tumors.614. EBNA3C deficient tumors had increased T-cell infiltration and upregulation of the type 1 interferon response, suggesting additional EBNA3C immunomodulation roles in vivo. EBV deficient for either EBNA3A or 3C establishes persistent infection but fails to induce tumors in humanized NOD-SCID mouse models.521 A hypomorphic mutation that allows expression only of small amounts of an EBNA3A N-terminal deletion mutant lacking the first 14 residues caused lymphomas at rates similar to wild-type EBV, albeit with delayed kinetics.615 EBNA3B is not critical for EBV-driven primary B cell conversion to LCLs.13,154,729 EBNA3B epitopes are frequently recognized by cytotoxic T lymphocytes. Interestingly, humanized mouse infection by EBNA3B-deficient EBV causes aggressive monomorphic lymphomas, which are not infiltrated by EBV-reactive T-cells despite their expansion in this model.781 EBNA3B knockout deficient B-cells secreted less CXCL10, a chemokine that attracts T-cells, a phenotype that was also observed in EBNA3B-deficient LCLs. Thus, EBNA3B can be considered to have tumor suppressor roles in vivo, perhaps safeguarding against malignancy during the establishment of latency.
<H3>LMP1

LMP1 was identified by Elliott Kieff’s group as the most abundant viral mRNA in lymphoblastoid B-cells.199 LMP1 mimicks CD40 signaling to subvert a major B/T-cell communication pathway506, and is essential for in vitro B cell conversion into LCLs.173,332,334,346 As described in detail below, LMP1 constitutively activates NF-B, mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K), JAK/STAT, interferon regulatory factor (IRF) and SUMOylation pathways in a ligand-independent manner. In single gene transfer experiments using heterologous promoters, LMP1 has transforming or "oncogene" effects in continuous rodent fibroblast cell lines.757 LMP1 alters Rat-1 or NIH 3T3 cell morphology, enables growth in medium supplemented with low serum, causes loss of contact inhibition, and enhances growth as tumors in nude mice. Rat-1 or Balb/c 3T3 cells also lose anchorage dependence and grow in soft agar after LMP1 expression.571,757 The growth of Balb/c 3T3 cells in soft agar correlates quantitatively with the extent of LMP1 expression up to the levels ordinarily expressed in LCLs.

LMP1 is transcribed from one of two viral promoters separated by ~600 bp. In B cells, LMP1 is encoded by a 2.8-kb mRNA, which initiates from the ED-L1 promoter that is dependent on EBNA2.312 ED-L1 can also be activated independently of EBNA2 by cellular factors, such as the STATs, IRF7, NF-B, ATF4, PAX5, AP-2 and EBF1.108,385,166,520,536,769 Enhancement of LMP1 expression up to 200-fold can be mediated by the EBNA1-dependent transcriptional enhancer FR in oriP acting across the fused TRs220, potentially by the long-range oriP enhancer looping to the LMP1 promoter.719 LMP1 transcripts are detectable within 48 hours of B-cell infection and steadily increase over the first two weeks post-infection.588 LMP1 also activates the unfolded protein response to drive its own synthesis, and LMP1 levels in individual cells vary by over 100-fold in clonal LCL cultures.385 Highly elevated MYC levels early after EBV infection dampen B-cell LMP1 expression587, potentially through interaction with a cis-acting E-box site353.

In epithelial cells, LMP1 transcription is mediated by the upstream L1-TR promoter that initiates transcription from multiple TATA-less sites in the nearest copy of TR, resulting in a 3.5 kb transcript with a long untranslated 5' exon.227,558 Transcription is in part dependent on the cellular factors Sp1 and STAT3.227,558 LMP2A can negatively regulate the expression of LMP1 from this promoter696, whereas TR copy number varies inversely to LMP1 expression.603 The LMP1 ORF has two short introns.33,198 Epithelial cell differentiation regulates LMP1 expression, where the host transcription factors KLF4 and BLIMP1 jointly upregulate LMP1 through co-activation of the two LMP1 promoters.528 L1-TR is active in nasopharyngeal carcinoma and interestingly also in Hodgkin lymphoma.108,603

LMP1 induces many of the changes usually associated with EBV infection of primary B cells or with antigen activation of primary B cells, including homotypic adhesion, villous projections, increased vimentin expression, increased cell surface expression of CD23, CD39, CD40, CD44, and class II MHC, increased IL-10 expression, decreased expression of CD10, and increased expression of the cell adhesion molecules LFA-1, ICAM-1, and LFA-3.2 LMP1 also activates adhesion molecules to promote homotypic adhesion. LMP1 is not required for EBV-induced B-cell outgrowth over the first week of infection.573,588 EBV-infected cells become dependent on LMP1 and NF-B approximately 1-2 weeks post infection in vitro588, and conditional LMP1 inactivation or NF-B blockade triggers LCL growth arrest and apoptosis.79-82,346

Cryo-electron microscopy revealed that LMP1 forms stable homodimers as well as higher-order filamentous oligomers.279 Reverse genetic experiments defined key LMP1 domains important for B-cell transformation (Fig. 71.12). Deletion of the 24 residue N-terminal cytoplasmic tail reduces transforming efficiency, possibly because of effects on trafficking or stability.298 The LMP1 six transmembrane domains induce intra- and inter-molecular association that drive LMP1 signaling. The 200 residue LMP1 C-terminal tail contains three signaling regions and is critical for B-cell transformation. Of these, CTAR/Transformation Effector Site (TES) 1 and 2 are critical for EBV-mediated B-cell transformation into LCLs.299,332-334 An EBV recombinant lacking CTAR1 residues 185-211 is unable to transform primary human cells into LCLs in vitro, suggesting obligatory CTAR1 role(s).299,332-334 Interestingly, recombinant EBV that expresses only the first 231 LMP1 residues and therefore lacks CTAR2/TES2 and CTAR3 transforms primary B-cells into LCLs, so long as they are either grown on fibroblast feeder layers or high-titers of EBV are used.299,332-334 While deletion of LMP1 residues encompassing CTAR3 does not abrogate B-cell growth transformation297,299, in vivo roles remain possible. Indeed, CTAR3 alters cell migration and promotes the establishment of latency.38,40,296 CTAR3 associates with the SUMO ligase Ubc9, which itself is induced by LMP1 CTAR1/2.40,217,628

LMP1 activates two NF-B pathways, termed canonical and non-canonical. CTAR2/TES2 associates with TRADD, TNIK and TRAF6 to initiate canonical NF-B signaling.226,297,431,647,649,659. TRAF6 recruitment is essential for CTAR2/TES2-mediated canonical NF-κB activation226 and its association with LMP1 is supported by the host adaptor protein p62.764 In turn, TRAF6 activates the kinase TAK1, which phosphorylates the IB kinase (IKK) IKK765 (Fig. 71.12). The linear ubiquitin assembly complex (LUBAC) also plays a key role in IKK activation.224 IKK phosphorylates IB, promoting its ubiquitination by -TRCP and proteasomal turnover. IB degradation releases dimeric NF-B transcription factors, typically RelA:p50 or cRel:p50 for nuclear translocation and to target gene activation. CRISPR loss-of-function analysis identified TRAF6, TAK1, LUBAC, IKK, RelA and cRel as important for LCL growth and survival.443

CTAR1 induces a complex NF-κB response, as determined by electopherectic mobility shift assay.331,493 Recombinant LMP1 lacking CTAR2 efficiently induces NF-κB target genes including ICAM-1 at levels similar to wild-type virus.299,332-334 Recombinant LMP1 lacking TES2/CTAR2 signaling is highly impaired for upregulation of the anti-apoptotic protein cFLIP.496 Perhaps relatedly, LCLs survive CRISPR LMP1 KO if rescued by cDNA encoding LMP1 in which only TES1, but not TES2, signals.496 LMP1 CTAR1/TES1 uses a PXQXT motif to recruit TRAFs 1, 2, 3 and 5.168,506,806 PxQxT motifs were subsequently found to also be used by immune receptors including CD40. CTAR1 activates non-canonical NF-B inducing kinase (NIK), which activates the IKKα kinase432. IKK phosphorylates p100, triggering production of the active p52 NF-B subunit. p52 homodimers or heterodimers then regulate target genes. p52 is necessary for LCL growth and survival, though interestingly RelB is not, perhaps because of redundancy.443 Association with TRAF1 enhances CTAR1/TES1 activation of the canonical NF-B pathway, where TRAF1:TRAF2 heterotrimers recruit LUBAC and lysine-63 ubiquitin ligases to activate TAK1.235

In epithelial cells, a key LMP1 target is the epithelial growth factor receptor (EGFR), which is induced by CTAR1 signaling through NF-B, BCL3 and STAT3. LMP1-activated STAT3 induces BCL3, which co-occupies the EGFR promoter together with p50 homodimers.367,726 Similarly, LMP1 suppression of the junctional protein plakoglobin influences a cadherin switch, with effects on cell migration relevant to nasopharyngeal carcinoma metastasis.655 LMP1 also blocks p53-mediated apoptosis through induction of the NF-B target gene A20216 and enhances YAP/TAZ signaling in oral keratinocytes to support cellular proliferation and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition.664

Constitutive LMP1 activation of canonical and non-canonical pathways gives rise to a complex genomic NF-B binding landscape. Indeed, as many as 13 NF-B dimeric transcription factors may form in LCL nuclei.816 NF-B occupies 73% of LCL active enhancers, but does not readily reflect the two NF-B pathway paradigm. Rather, 11 distinct NF-B profiles were present at enhancers and ten at promoters, suggesting that there is significant cross-talk between the canonical and non-canonical NF-B pathways at the level of the host genome.816 NF-B targets critical for LCL survival include c-FLIP443 and BCL2 family members.586,257 Proteomic analysis found that >80% of LMP1 gene targets were encoded by genes identified to be targeted by NF-B.165 LMP1 further influences host target gene regulation through effects on PARylation.460

LMP1 strongly activates the JNK, p38, and ERK MAP and PI3 kinase pathways.345,766 Experiments with dominant negative JNK or with JNK chemical inhibitors indicate that JNK activation is critical for LMP1 effects on transformed cell growth. TAK1 plays multiple roles in MAPK activation, including a kinase-independent role in LMP1 signaling complex formation that contributes to downstream TPL2 and JNK kinase activation. This does not appear to be shared with CD40.753 TRAF1 enables LMP1 TES1 to also strongly activate MAPK pathways.235 Also differing from CD40, LMP1 activates IRF7.794 LMP1 CTAR2 binds to IRF7 and induces K63-linked ubiquitination in a RIP1 and TRAF6 dependent fashion.535,537,686 LMP1 induces IRF7 sumoylation39, which limits IRF7 DNA binding and transcriptional activation and thereby potentially limits innate immune responses. LMP1 associates with the PI3 kinase through CTAR1.160,376 CTAR1 but not CTAR2 is necessary for LMP1-mediated rodent and human fibroblast transformation through the activation of the kinases PI3K and AKT.447 The cytoskeleton protein vimentin, which associates with LMP1, is important for LMP1-mediated PI3K/AKT pathway activation.475

LMP1 oligomers form patches at the plasma membrane and endosomal membrane sites.410 LMP1 signals from cholesterol rich membrane microdomains termed lipid rafts327, and egress from the endoplasmic reticulum is necessary for LMP1 signaling.375 The Rab family protein Rab13 is induced by EBV within the first days of B-cell infection, colocalizes with LMP1 and LMP2A, and has key roles in their intracellular trafficking to signaling sites.768

Mouse models have highlighted LMP1 oncogenicity. Transgenic LMP1 expression causes B-cell lymphoproliferative disease in mice.366,811 Mice expressing an LMP1/CD40 chimera, in which the LMP1 TMs drive constitutive signaling from the CD40 cytoplasmic tail develop B-cell lymphomas as result of hyperactive CD40 signaling.254-598 By contrast, transgenic mice expressing a chimeric CD40 extracellular and transmembrane domain fused to the LMP1 C-terminal tail are relatively normal. Immunoglobulin heavy chain promoter and enhancer driven LMP1 expression results in B cell hyperplasia and lymphomas in aged mice.366 By contrast, when expressed from a CD19 promoter, LMP1-positive cells are recognized and destroyed by T and NK cell responses.811 T cell depletion causes fatal lymphoproliferative disease, which was also seen in mice with conditional LMP1 and LMP2A co-expression following T and NK cell suppression.786,495 LMP1 is not absolutely necessary for EBV-driven lymphomagenesis in a cord blood humanized mouse model, apparently because CD40 signaling may compensate to some degree.440 Likewise, EBV deficienct for LMP1 and LMP2A could cause lymphoma in a cord blood-humanized mouse model, albeit at reduced frequency from wild-type EBV.439 LMP1 expression also induces potent cytotoxic CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell responses in murine models, including against tumor associated antigens.124

LMP1 remodels host metabolic pathways, in part through effects on PARP1-mediated post-translational modification of target genes, including hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF-1a), and by LMP1 upgregulation of the lactate exporters MCT1 and 454. These potentiates glycolytic Warburg metabolism.285 PARP1 inhibition causes accumulation of repressive histone methylation marks and results in EBV lytic reactivation, likely through effects on the BZLF1 promoter.435 EBV similarly upregulates glycolysis in transformed epithelial cells, and EBV-driven cell metabolism remodeling likely has key roles in nasopharyngeal carcinoma pathogenesis.813
<H3>LMP2A and LMP2B

LMP2A acts as a broad inducer of cellular signal transducers in part by acting as a B cell receptor mimic but also by rewiring B cell signal transduction resulting in differential phosphorylation of kinases, phosphatases, adaptor proteins, transcription factors such as NF-B and TCF3, as well as widespread changes in the transcriptional output of LMP2A-expressing B cells100,203 (Fig. 71.13). As a result, the two EBV latent membrane proteins provide two signals that are essential for normal B cell development and function – LMP1 providing a CD40 like-signal and LMP2A a BCR like-signal. Together, LMP1 and LMP2A direct EBV infected B cells to the memory B cell compartment where EBV establishes a latent infection. LMP2B is related to LMP2A, but lacks the amino terminal domain required for LMP2A signaling function (Fig. 71.13). LMP2A and LMP2B in latency III are expressed from unique EBNA2 responsive promoters with RBP-Jκ and PU.1 binding sites.479,634,833

In latency IIa, in which EBNA2 is not expressed, LMP2A may autoactivate its own expression through Notch providing a mechanism for expression independent of EBNA2.18 The LMP2A first exon encodes 119 N-terminal cytosolic amino acids that precede a methionine, which is the translational start site for the LMP2B mRNA. LMP2A and 2B mRNAs share the remaining exons which encode 12 transmembrane (TM) spanning domains separated by short reverse turns and a 27 amino acid C-terminal cytosolic domain383,634 (Fig. 71.13). Several studies have suggested that LMP2B can augment LMP1 signaling and negatively regulate the function of LMP2A.600,601,618 LMP2A colocalizes with LMP1 in patches in membranes of latently infected B lymphocytes.422 LMP2A is palmitylated267,329,466 and associates with lipid rafts which is likely important for initial contact with Src family tyrosine kinases such as Lyn. Along with lipid raft association, Lyn is likely recruited to LMP2A by the amino acids DQSL in LMP2A C-terminal cytoplasmic domain, which is similar to the amino acids DCSM in the BCR-associated protein Ig-α. This interaction is required for the phosphorylation of LMP2A tyrosines found within the LMP2A amino terminal domain, including an ITAM motif which binds the Syk tyrosine kinase via two Syk SH2 domains.71,487,619 This results in the activation of a variety of cellular signal transducers, including RAS, PI3K, Btk, BLNK, Akt, mTor, and MAPK100,186,482,483,487,502,707 (Fig. 71.13). However, the majority of LMP2A-driven signaling events differ from those induced by B-cell receptor stimulation to optimize cell survival and transformation, including by counteracting MYC-induced apoptosis.202 LMP2A also rewires B-cell metabolism to increase ATP generation.294

The LMP2A N-terminus has two PPPPY motifs which bind WW domains of Nedd4 family ubiquitin ligases, such as AIP4/Itchy, WWP2, Nedd4, or Nedd4-2.290,292 This interaction results in the ubiquitination and degradation of LMP2A and LMP2A associated proteins.

LMP2A and 2B have been extensively mutated within the EBV genome indicating that LMP2A and LMP2B are not absolutely essential for transforming primary B lymphocytes in culture, but in some cases can provide a growth advantage.60,451,452,573,612,693 Compatible with this observation, CRISPR/Cas9 dependency screens have shown LMP2A targets such as Syk, Btk, BLNK, PI3 Kinase, and cell cycle regulators are important for LCL growth in culture.442 LMP2A, like LMP1 provides survival and differentiation signals to B cells in vivo. This was first shown using transgenic mice where LMP2A expression in transgenic mice was directed to B cells, which allowed BCR negative B cells to escape from the bone marrow and colonize peripheral lymphoid organs, bypassing normal B cell developmental checkpoints by constitutive activation of BCR signal transducers.19,87 The LMP2A effect is also evident in RAG1 KO mice and a number of proteins important for BCR signaling, such as Syk, Btk, and BLNK. The LMP2A ITAM is important for this effect.186,482,483 Thus, LMP2A has a role in latency type II infected lymphocytes in enhancing B cell survival through activation of B cell signal transducers.

In transgenic mice, high level LMP2A expression results in B-1 cells in bone marrow, spleen, and the periphery, whereas low level expression results in spontaneous germinal centers.96,291 More recent studies using engineered mice confirm the role of LMP2A and LMP1 to mimic signals B cells receive in a germinal center reaction. LMP2A provides an antigen independent signal and T-cell help signal mediated by LMP1 allows antigen-independent proliferation.495,825

In murine models of Burkitt lymphoma using a myc transgene expressed in B cells, LMP2A has been shown to dramatically accelerate tumor development, by bypassing the requirement of mutation of the p53 pathway45 and by activating the cell cycle through increasing p27kip1 degradation.687 Remarkably, tumors derived from LMP2A/MYC mice share a similar pattern of gene expression with MYC tumors derived from transgenic mice, despite the absence of p53 pathway mutations in LMP2A/MYC mice.46 LMP2A expression is detected as mRNA transcripts and protein in Burkitt and Hodgkin lymphoma biopsies. Like Burkitt lymphoma, Hodgkin lymphoma exhibits latency II, which includes EBNA1, LMP1 and LMP2A. EBV-associated diffuse large B cell lymphoma shows latency II or III, including LMP1 and LMP2A. In HIV/AIDS-related lymphomas, EBV latent gene expression is heterogeneous, and LMP1 and LMP2A, in addition to EBNA2 and EBNA3A/B/C are variably expressed.

Constitutive activation of important cellular signal transducers by LMP2A is likely important in the pathogenesis of EBV-associated malignancies. An important role for LMP2A in classical Hodkgin lymphoma can be surmised, since crippling mutations in the immunoglobulin genes are found, which would normally result in the death of these cells. LMP2A and LMP1 are uniformly expressed, providing a role for LMP2A and LMP1 in classical Hodgkin lymphoma, by allowing bypass of apoptotic signals that should normally result in cell death due to the absence of the expression of the BCR. Also in support of a role of LMP2A in classical Hodkin lymphoma, LMP2A expression during B cell development in mice results in decreased expression of E2A, EBF, and Pax-5, which are important for normal B cell development.582,583 Furthermore, LMP2A activates Notch, which alters B cell identity.20 Similar changes and loss of B cell identity are observed in classical Hodgkin lymphoma.

LMP2A is an important factor in NPC and gastric carcinoma.205 LMP2A expression in epithelial cells line results in hyperproliferation in raft cultures, alterations in differentiation, increased cloning efficiency in soft agar, and promotes epithelial cell spreading and migration.12,212,362,429,648 AKT activation increases β-catenin and cell growth through the LMP2A ITAM and PY motif.504,505,560 In summary, LMP2A, like LMP1, delivers a potent cell survival signal to B lymphocytes and epithelial cells, and may provide a therapeutic target in EBV-associated cancers.
<H3>EBERs

EBERs 1 and 2 are transcribed by RNA pol III in a manner enhanced by EBNA1 as non-polyadenylated transcripts of 167 and 172 nucleotides, respectively. The EBERs have intragenic A and B box transcriptional control regions common to pol III transcripts.675 At steady state levels in latently infected B lymphocytes, the EBERs are the most most abundant viral RNAs, reaching 1-5 million copies per cell.
